zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Balad
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لا أُقْسِمُ بِهَذا البَلَدِ﴾: by "the town" here Mecca is meant. The meaning is: ”أُقْسِمُ بِهَذا البَلَدِ“ ("I swear by this town"), and ”لا“ was inserted for emphasis (tawkīd), just as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿لِئَلا يَعْلَمَ أهْلُ الكِتابِ﴾ [al-Ḥadīd: 29] ("so that the People of the Book may know"). It was also read: ”لَأُقْسِمُ بِهَذا البَلَدِ“, in which case the lām is the lām of the oath and of emphasis. This reading is rare, and it is far-fetched in Arabic, because the lām of the oath does not enter a future-tense verb unless the nūn [of emphasis] is with it: you say ”لَأضْرِبَنَّ زَيْدًا“ ("I will surely strike Zayd"), and ”لَأضْرِبُ“ is not permitted when you mean the present. And Sībawayh and al-Khalīl claimed that this lām enters together with ”إنَّ“, and so it is made sufficient in the chapter of ”إنَّ“: you say ”إنِّي لَأُحِبُّكَ“ ("I surely love you").

zajjaj:2-2.t: And the meaning of ﴿وَأنْتَ حِلٌّ بِهَذا البَلَدِ﴾ ("and you are free [of restriction] in this town"): Mecca was made lawful for the Prophet, peace be upon him, for an hour of the day, and it was not lawful for anyone before him nor for anyone after him. And the meaning of ”أُحِلَّتْ لَهُ“ ("it was made lawful for him") is: its game was made lawful for him, and that its fresh herbage be cut and its trees be lopped. One says: ”رَجُلٌ حِلٌّ“, ”حَلالٌ“ and ”مُحَلٌّ“ (a man in the non-sacral state); and likewise ”رَجُلٌ حَرامٌ“, ”حِرْمٌ“ and ”مُحْرِمٌ“ (a man in the sacral state).

zajjaj:3-3.t: And His saying: ﴿وَوالِدٍ وما ولَدَ﴾ ("and by a begetter and what he begot"): it has come in the exegesis that its meaning is Adam and his offspring; and its meaning has also come as: every begetter and every one begotten.

zajjaj:4-4.t: And His saying: ﴿لَقَدْ خَلَقْنا الإنْسانَ في كَبَدٍ﴾: this is the answer to the oath (jawāb al-qasam). The meaning is: "I swear by these things: We have certainly created the human being in kabad", that is, he endures hardship (yukābidu) in his affairs in this world and the Hereafter. And it was said: ﴿فِي كَبَدٍ﴾ means he was created upright, walking on his two legs, while all other things and animals are not upright. And it was said ﴿فِي كَبَدٍ﴾: the human being was created in his mother's womb with his head toward her head, and when she wishes to give birth the head turns downward.

zajjaj:5-5.t: And His saying: ﴿أنْ لَنْ يَقْدِرَ عَلَيْهِ أحَدٌ﴾ ("that no one has power over him"): this, it has come in the exegesis, is a man who was extremely strong. An ʿUkāẓī hide used to be spread out for him, and he would stand on it and it would be torn apart, so that nothing came out from under his feet except in pieces, because of his strength. He was called Kalada. So it was said: "Does he think, because of his strength, that no one has power over him, and that he will not be resurrected?!" And it was said: "[Does he think] that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has no power over him?" — because he did not believe in the Resurrection.

zajjaj:6-6.t: ﴿يَقُولُ أهْلَكْتُ مالا لُبَدًا﴾ ("he says: I have squandered heaps of wealth"). It was read: ”أهْلَكْتُ مالًا لُبَدًا“, and it is also read: ”لُبَّدًا“. The meaning of ”لُبَدًا“ is "much", part of it matted (lubbida) onto part. The pattern ”فُعَلٌ“ is for abundance: one says ”رَجُلٌ حُطَمٌ“ when a man smashes (ḥaṭm) a great deal. And whoever reads ”لُبَّدًا“, it is the plural of ”لابِدٌ“.

zajjaj:7-7.t: ﴿أيَحْسَبُ أنْ لَمْ يَرَهُ أحَدٌ﴾ ("does he think that no one saw him?"): that is, does he think that what he spent is not counted against him? And in the discourse there is evidence that he claimed he had spent a great deal which did not benefit him.

zajjaj:8-9.t: And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿ألَمْ نَجْعَلْ لَهُ عَيْنَيْنِ﴾ ﴿وَلِسانًا وشَفَتَيْنِ﴾ ﴿وَهَدَيْناهُ النَّجْدَيْنِ﴾ [al-Balad: 10] ("Have We not made for him two eyes, and a tongue and two lips, and guided him to the two highways?"): that is, have We not done for him that by which one infers that Allah is able to resurrect him and to count against him what he does?!

zajjaj:10-10.t: ﴿وَهَدَيْناهُ النَّجْدَيْنِ﴾: the two clear ways. ”اَلنَّجْدُ“ is raised ground. So the meaning is: "Have We not made known to him the way of good and the way of evil, as clear as the clarity of two elevated roads?!"

zajjaj:11-11.t:
And His saying: ﴿فَلا اقْتَحَمَ العَقَبَةَ﴾: the meaning is ”فَلَمْ يَقْتَحِمِ العَقَبَةَ“ ("but he did not attempt the steep ascent").
Just as He said: ﴿فَلا صَدَّقَ ولا صَلّى﴾ [al-Qiyāma: 31] ("for he neither affirmed nor prayed"). Here He mentioned ”لا“ only once, whereas the Arabs rarely speak in such a position without ”لا“ twice or more; you would hardly say ”لا حَيَّيْتَنِي“ meaning ”ما حَيَّيْتَنِي“ ("you did not greet me"), but if you said "[لا] حَيَّيْتَنِي ولا زُرْتَنِي" ("you neither greeted me nor visited me") it would be sound. [Translator's note: the source reads «حَيَّيْتَنِي ولا زُرْتَنِي» without the first «لا»; the argument requires «لا حَيَّيْتَنِي ولا زُرْتَنِي».] The meaning [of the repeated lā] in ﴿فَلا اقْتَحَمَ العَقَبَةَ﴾ is present: a second ”لا“ is as if it were in the discourse, because His saying ﴿ثُمَّ كانَ مِنَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ [al-Balad: 17] ("then he was of those who believed") points to the meaning ”فَلا اقْتَحَمَ العَقَبَةَ ولا آمَنَ“ ("he neither attempted the steep ascent nor believed").

zajjaj:13-14.t: It was read: ﴿فَكُّ رَقَبَةٍ﴾ ﴿أوْ إطْعامٌ في يَوْمٍ ذِي مَسْغَبَةٍ﴾ ("the freeing of a slave, or feeding on a day of hunger"), and it was read: ”فَكَّ رَقَبَةً أوْ أطْعَمَ في يَوْمٍ ذِي مَسْغَبَةٍ“ ("he freed a slave or fed on a day of hunger"), and both are permissible. Whoever said ﴿فَكُّ رَقَبَةٍ﴾, the meaning is: "attempting the steep ascent is the freeing of a slave or feeding"; and whoever read ”فَكَّ رَقَبَةً“, it is construed according to the sense. And ”اَلْمَسْغَبَةُ“ is famine.

zajjaj:15-15.t:
And His saying: ﴿يَتِيمًا ذا مَقْرَبَةٍ﴾: its meaning is "possessed of kinship". You say: ”زَيْدٌ ذُو قَرابَتِي، وذُو مَقْرَبَتِي“ ("Zayd is one of my kin"), whereas ”زَيْدٌ قَرابَتِي“ is ugly, because ”اَلْقَرابَةُ“ is the maṣdar (verbal noun). The poet said:
يَبْكِي عَلَيْهِ غَرِيبٌ لَيْسَ يَعْرِفُهُ ∗∗∗ وذُو قَرابَتِهِ في الحَيِّ مَسْرُورُ
(A stranger who does not know him weeps over him, while his kinsman in the tribe is glad.)
And His saying: ﴿ذا مَتْرَبَةٍ﴾ [al-Balad: 16]: He means that, from his poverty, he has cleaved to the dust.

zajjaj:17-17.t: And His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ كانَ مِنَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾: its meaning is: "When he did that, and had bound himself to faith, and then remained steadfast upon his faith." ﴿وَتَواصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ﴾ ("and enjoined one another to patience"): that is, upon obedience to Allah, and patience in refraining from entering into acts of disobedience to Him. Then, along with that, he was of those who enjoin one another to compassion; those are the people of good fortune (al-yumn) for themselves, that is, they were bringers of blessing upon themselves, not of ill omen.

zajjaj:19-19.t: ﴿والَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِآياتِنا هم أصْحابُ المَشْأمَةِ﴾: that is, they are the bringers of ill omen upon themselves. We seek refuge in Allah from the Fire.

zajjaj:20-20.t: And His saying: ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ نارٌ مُؤْصَدَةٌ﴾ ("over them is a Fire closed in"): it is also read without hamza; its meaning is "closed over". One says ”آصَدْتُ البابَ“ and ”أوْصَدْتُهُ“ ("I closed the door") when I have shut it.
